The control test passes only because it compares the code to the params file this change raised to 16.

The cited EXC-0210 is scoped to component mortgage.session, not any payments component, so it is out of scope. The only payments SES-1 exception, EXC-0141, expired 2026-09-19 and covered batch service accounts only. No valid exception covers the deviation.

Ticket CHG-24034 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager erik.brandt at 2026-10-13T07:53Z, before the change opened at 14:53Z. Its components (payments.policy, payments.controls-data) cover both touched paths.
Code review approval by mara.costa, a payments change_approver and a different person from the author jonah.weiss.
The code_review and control_owner approvals both name the head commit 63831d6, the change's only commit.

The CI run on head 63831d6 succeeded: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped, including the registered SES-1 control test (exhaustive). I could not re-run it locally (pytest not installed), and the report's timestamp is later than the review time.
controls/payments/policy-params.json is a protected path. The change has a control_owner approval on head from rachel.stein (controls-office), who is outside the author's payments-eng team.
No ledger entry covers code this change alters (the entries cover payments.py, audit.py and mortgage files), so no earlier evidence lapses.

summary: The change raises payments' privileged idle timeout from 15 to 16 minutes, breaking SES-1's approved bound of 15 minutes or less. The risk acceptance it cites, EXC-0210, covers the mortgage.session component, not payments, and no other valid exception applies, so EXC-1 is not met. The SES-1 control test passes only because it compares the code to the params file the change also raised. The process records (ticket, independent review, control-owner approval, CI on head) are in order, but a refuted product obligation requires rejection.
